breadcrumb: Std 6 Social Science Term-II (English) — Civics Unit 2: The Constitution of India — Boxed notes (தெரிந்து தெளிவோம் / Do you know)

questions.quote: When the Congress met at Lahore in 1929, the members of the Congress unofficially declared the same day as the Day of Poorna Swaraj. The next year, 26th January 1930 was celebrated as the Independence Day.

en.q: At which Congress session of 1929 was 26 January declared the Day of Poorna Swaraj?
en.explanation: 26 January 1930 was celebrated as Independence Day; the same day was later chosen for the Republic Day.

ta.q: 1929இல் எங்கு நடந்த காங்கிரஸ் மாநாட்டில் ஜனவரி 26 பூரண சுயராஜ்ய நாளாக அறிவிக்கப்பட்டது?
ta.explanation: 1930 ஜனவரி 26 சுதந்திர நாளாகக் கொண்டாடப்பட்டது; அதே நாள் பின்னர் குடியரசு நாளாயிற்று.

questions.quote: The Constitution is an authentic document containing the basic ideas, principles and laws of a country. It also defines the rights and duties of citizens. The Constitution of India is the ultimate law.

en.q: The ultimate law of India that all must abide by is the ______.
en.explanation: It explains the structure, powers and duties of government bodies and lists the rights and duties of citizens. (The Indian Penal Code has been replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.)

ta.q: இந்தியாவில் அனைவரும் கடைப்பிடிக்க வேண்டிய உயர்ந்த சட்டம் ______.
ta.explanation: அரசுக் கட்டமைப்பு, அதிகாரம், குடிமக்களின் உரிமை, கடமைகளை அது கூறுகிறது. (இந்தியத் தண்டனைச் சட்டத்துக்குப் பதிலாக பாரதிய நியாய சம்ஹிதா 2023 வந்துள்ளது.)

questions.quote: In 1946, nearly 389 members of the constituent Assembly came together to frame the Constitution of India. The Chairman of the committee was Mr. Rajendra Prasad. Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabai Patel, Moulana Azad, S. Radhakrishnan, Vijayalakshmi Pandit and Sarojini Naidu were members.

en.q: Which of the following was a member of the Constituent Assembly?
en.explanation: Other members included Nehru, Patel, Maulana Azad, S. Radhakrishnan and Vijayalakshmi Pandit.

ta.explanation: நேரு, பட்டேல், மௌலானா ஆசாத், ராதாகிருஷ்ணன், விஜயலட்சுமி பண்டிட் ஆகியோரும் உறுப்பினர்கள்.

questions.quote: The constitutions of nearly 60 countries including the UK, USA, former USSR, France, Switzerland etc., were thoroughly examined and their best features have been adopted by our constitution. Nearly 2000 amendments were made before the draft was finalised.

en.q: The constitutions of about how many countries were examined while framing the Indian Constitution?
en.explanation: The UK, USA, former USSR, France and Switzerland were among them.

ta.q: இந்திய அரசியலமைப்பை உருவாக்கும்போது ஏறத்தாழ எத்தனை நாடுகளின் அரசியலமைப்புகள் ஆராயப்பட்டன?
ta.explanation: பிரிட்டன், அமெரிக்கா, முன்னாள் சோவியத், பிரான்ஸ், சுவிட்சர்லாந்து உள்ளிட்டவை.

questions.quote: The constitution was accepted by the Constituent Assembly. So, 26th November is celebrated as the Day of the Constitution. They spent almost 64 lakhs to frame the constitution.

en.q: Approximately how much was spent to frame the Constitution of India?
en.explanation: The work took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days.

ta.q: இந்திய அரசியலமைப்பை உருவாக்க ஏறத்தாழ எவ்வளவு செலவானது?

questions.quote: The Constitution of India provides a Parliamentary form of Government, both at the centre and the state. In a Parliamentary System, the Executive is collectively responsible to the Legislature. The party which has the majority forms the government.

en.q: In a Parliamentary System, the Executive is collectively responsible to the ______.
en.explanation: The party which has the majority forms the government.

ta.q: நாடாளுமன்ற முறையில் நிர்வாகத்துறை கூட்டுப் பொறுப்புடன் ______ க்குப் பதிலளிக்கும்.

questions.quote: What is the meaning of 'Secular'? The law allows all the citizens of a country, the right to follow different faith and religious beliefs. All citizens enjoy the freedom of worship. The country does not have a religion of its own.

en.q: A secular state is one in which ______.
options: all religions are banned from public life
the state has no religion and all are free to worship
the state follows Hinduism as its official religion
only the majority religion is protected by law
en.explanation: All religions in our country hold the same status.

options: எல்லா மதங்களும் பொது வாழ்வில் தடை செய்யப்படும்
அரசுக்குத் தனி மதம் இல்லை; அனைவரும் வழிபடலாம்
ta.explanation: நம் நாட்டில் அனைத்து மதங்களுக்கும் சம தகுதி.

questions.quote: Fundamental rights: Right to Equality, Right to freedom, Right against exploitation, Right to freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, Right to Constitutional Remedies.

en.q: How many Fundamental Rights are listed in the lesson?
en.explanation: They are Equality, Freedom, against Exploitation, Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights and Constitutional Remedies.

ta.explanation: சமத்துவம், சுதந்திரம், சுரண்டலுக்கெதிரான உரிமை, சமயச் சுதந்திரம், பண்பாட்டு-கல்வி உரிமை, அரசியலமைப்புத் தீர்வு உரிமை.

questions.quote: When the Constitution was drafted, there were 395 articles in 22 parts and 8 schedules. At present our Indian Constitution contains 448 articles in 25 parts and 12 schedules.

en.q: When the Constitution was drafted it had ______ articles in 22 parts and 8 schedules.
en.explanation: At present it contains 448 articles in 25 parts and 12 schedules.

ta.q: அரசியலமைப்பு வரையப்பட்டபோது 22 பகுதிகளும் 8 அட்டவணைகளும் கொண்ட ______ உறுப்புகள் இருந்தன.
